page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, alongside standard x86 instruction sets including AVX, BMI2, and SHA-NI, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware specifications show that ecs.c6a.2xlarge includes no integrated GPUs and comes without local instance storage, requiring remote cloud storage volumes for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is set to 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached by default. Benchmark performance metrics place the instance consistently in the middle tier across standard workloads, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 5025.0, a PassMark CPU score of 10249.39, and a Redis SET throughput of 7.44 million operations per second. However, heavy synthetic execution under stress-ng places its single-core and multi-core outputs in the lower percentiles.

Uncached memory bandwidth tests demonstrate lower-tier throughput at 32.16 GB/sec for 256MB reads and 16.75 GB/sec for writes, contrasting with average performance for small cached blocks at 395.92 GB/sec. Given its compute-focused 1:2 resource allocation and lack of local storage, the instance serves as a cost-efficient option for horizontal computing architectures, software compilation, medium-load web servers, and stateless processing tasks that do not rely on high memory density or low-latency disk IOPS.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance evaluations position the instance predominantly in the middle tier, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 10249.39 and static web serving throughput of 6.78 GB/sec, though raw synthetic stress tests and uncached memory writes demonstrate lower throughput relative to its peers. Due to its balance of compute threads and memory, ecs.c6a.2xlarge is well aligned with workloads such as continuous integration builds, distributed compute jobs, and standard web serving.
